#Intro

Morphological features such as substrate and color were not available for all sampled mats. Thus, the analysis of alpha and beta diversity were done separately to correctly assess the effect of substrate and color in the mats.

#Packages

```{r setup, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Only the packages used in this script are loaded.
# plyr is NOT loaded (it masks dplyr's summarise() and ignores group_by()).
# phyloseqCompanion is no longer needed: sample data is extracted with as(sample_data(), "data.frame").
# tidylog is loaded last so its dplyr wrappers are the active ones.
packages_used <- c("dplyr", "tibble", "ggplot2", "patchwork", "ggrepel",
                   "phyloseq", "vegan", "pairwiseAdonis", "MiscMetabar", "dunn.test",
                   "flextable", "officer", "tidylog")

suppressMessages(invisible(
  lapply(packages_used, library, character.only = TRUE)
))

missing_pkgs <- setdiff(packages_used, .packages())
if (length(missing_pkgs) == 0) {
  message("All packages loaded correctly")
} else {
  message("Packages that did not load: ", paste(missing_pkgs, collapse = ", "))
}
rm(packages_used, missing_pkgs)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE)

# Save numeric sequential copies of graphs in a path
auto_filename <- function(base, ext) {
  base <- sub(paste0("\\.", ext, "$"), "", base)  # remove extension if included
  full_path <- paste0(base, ".", ext)
  i <- 1
  while (file.exists(full_path)) {
    full_path <- paste0(base, "_", i, ".", ext)
    i <- i + 1
  }
  full_path
}

# Community matrix (samples as rows) from a phyloseq object, whatever its orientation
otu_matrix <- function(ps) {
  m <- as(otu_table(ps), "matrix")
  if (taxa_are_rows(ps)) m <- t(m)
  m
}

# Results table helper (rounded, optional "Source" column from row names)
to_table <- function(x, source_col = TRUE, digits = 4) {
  x <- as.data.frame(x)
  if (source_col) x <- rownames_to_column(x, "Source")
  mutate(x, across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, digits)))
}

message(paste0(utf8::as_utf8("\U0001f600"), " All good!"))
```

#Phyloseq load

Analysis based on the subset of mats based on the substrate they are on. Substrates that appear at least 3 times were considered for these analyses.

The categories used are:

-   cca-macroalgae (n=6), cca-rock (n=16), coral (n=3), macroalgae (n=17), mixed-benthos (n=17), rock (n=20), rubble (n=7), sed-rock (n=10), sponge (n=11)

Sediment (n=8) is not included in the subset below.

```{r stacked dataframes, echo=FALSE}
reef_tss <- readRDS("data/bcms_filtered&tss_reefs_raja2023.rds")
```

## Phyloseqs: morphotypes

Split for color morphotypes and substrates

```{r}
# Substrate categories present at least 3 times
# NOTE: sediment (n = 8) is not in this list; confirm this is intentional
morphotype_subs <- reef_tss %>% 
  subset_samples(direct_substrate %in% c("cca-macroalgae", "cca-rock", "coral", "macroalgae",
                                         "mixed-benthos", "rock", "rubble", "sed-rock", "sponge"))  

# Samples with a colour category. green_al and white are not included in the colour analysis
morphotype_col <- reef_tss %>%
  subset_samples(!is.na(site) &
                 !is.na(mat_color) &
                 !(mat_color %in% c("green_al", "white")))
```

# Frequencies

## Biotic_abiotic barplot stacked

Environmental and metadata (all samples)

```{r}
env.all <- as(sample_data(reef_tss), "data.frame") %>% 
  mutate(direct_substrate2 = na_if(trimws(direct_substrate2), ""))  
```


## Merged substrate stacked plots

```{r}
# 1. Valid category combinations
valid_levels <- c(
  "abiotic: rock",
  "abiotic: sed-rock",
  "abiotic: rubble",
  "mixed: cca-rock",
  "mixed: mixed-benthos",
  "biotic: cca-macroalgae",
  "biotic: coral",
  "biotic: macroalgae",
  "biotic: sponge"
)

# 2. Missing or unlisted categories become "NA"
env_nested <- env.all %>%
  mutate(
    raw_grouped    = paste(biotic_abiotic, direct_substrate2, sep = ": "),
    is_invalid     = is.na(biotic_abiotic) | is.na(direct_substrate2) | !(raw_grouped %in% valid_levels),
    biotic_abiotic = if_else(is_invalid, "NA", as.character(biotic_abiotic)),
    direct_substrate_grouped = if_else(is_invalid, "NA: NA", raw_grouped)
  ) %>%
  group_by(site_type, biotic_abiotic, direct_substrate_grouped) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(site_type) %>%
  mutate(prop = (n / sum(n)) * 100) %>%
  ungroup()

# 3. Factor ordering (bottom to top: NA -> mixed -> abiotic -> biotic)
env_nested <- env_nested %>%
  mutate(
    biotic_abiotic = factor(biotic_abiotic, levels = c("NA", "mixed", "abiotic", "biotic")),
    site_type      = factor(site_type, levels = c("reef", "lake")),
    direct_substrate_grouped = factor(direct_substrate_grouped, levels = c(valid_levels, "NA: NA"))
  )

# 4. Colours
custom_colors <- c(
  "abiotic: rock"          = "#8B4B2D",
  "abiotic: sed-rock"      = "#B9643C",
  "abiotic: rubble"        = "#D29274",
  "mixed: cca-rock"        = "#1F5B45",
  "mixed: mixed-benthos"   = "#349873",
  "biotic: cca-macroalgae" = "#463659",
  "biotic: coral"          = "#644e7e",
  "biotic: macroalgae"     = "#8267a2",
  "biotic: sponge"         = "#ab9ac1",
  "NA: NA"                 = "#CCCCCC"
)

# 5. Plot
subs_nested <- ggplot(env_nested, aes(y = biotic_abiotic, x = prop, fill = direct_substrate_grouped)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", color = "white") +
  facet_wrap(~ site_type, labeller = labeller(site_type = facet_labels_sitetype)) +
  labs(x = "Proportion (%)", y = "Category", fill = "Substrate (grouped)") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = custom_colors) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)

subs_nested

# Summary
substrate_summary <- env.all %>%
  dplyr::count(biotic_abiotic, direct_substrate2, name = "count") %>%
  mutate(percentage = round((count / sum(count)) * 100, 2)) %>%
  arrange(biotic_abiotic, desc(count))

substrate_summary
```

#------------------------------

#Alpha diversity

## Hill numbers

Package "MiscMetabar"

Hill numbers are the number of equiprobable species giving the same diversity value as the observed distribution.

-   Hill number 0: Species richness
-   Hill number 1: Exponential of Shannon Index
-   Hill number 2: Inverse of Simpson Index

## Direct Substrates

Data frames and Kruskal-Wallis tests

```{r shannon by direct substrate}
# Hill numbers, grouped by direct_substrate (the same variable as the Kruskal-Wallis test below;
# previously hill_pq() grouped by substrate_group)
hill_substrate <- hill_pq(morphotype_subs, "direct_substrate", add_points = TRUE, one_plot = FALSE)
hill_substrate[[1]]
hill_substrate[[2]]
hill_substrate[[3]]
hill_substrate[["tuckey"]]

# Dataframe (one row per sample)
hill_substratedf <- as.data.frame(hill_substrate[[2]][["data"]])
hill_substratedf$direct_substrate <- with(hill_substratedf, 
  reorder(direct_substrate, Hill_1, FUN = median))   # reorder by median for the plot

# Kruskal-Wallis
kw_substrate <- kruskal.test(Hill_1 ~ direct_substrate, data = hill_substratedf)
kw_substrate

# Dunn's test with Bonferroni adjustment
dunn_substrate <- dunn.test(hill_substratedf$Hill_1, hill_substratedf$direct_substrate,
                            method = "bonferroni")

dunn_substratedf <- data.frame(
  Comparison         = dunn_substrate$comparisons,
  Z_statistic        = dunn_substrate$Z,
  Unadjusted_p_value = dunn_substrate$P,
  Adjusted_p_value   = dunn_substrate$P.adjusted
) %>% 
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 4)))
dunn_substratedf
```

Save outputs as flex table

```{r}
dunn_substrateflex <- flextable(dunn_substratedf)
dunn_substrateflex

save_as_docx(dunn_substrateflex, path = "outputs/stats/dunn_substrate_alpha_results.docx")
write.csv(dunn_substratedf, "outputs/stats/dunn_substrate_alpha_results.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

<!-- TODO: the two statements below contradict each other (KW p = 0.02 vs "no significant differences"). Update both after rerunning kw_substrate. -->

Kruskal-Wallis test indicated overall differences among substrates (p = 0.02), but post-hoc Dunn's tests with Bonferroni correction did not identify significant pairwise differences. This suggests a general shift in diversity patterns without strong divergence between specific substrate types. Differences among groups are small and conservative corrections reduce the ability to detect them individually.

Plots

```{r hill substrate type plot}
caption_text <- paste0("Kruskal-Wallis \u03c7\u00b2 = ", round(kw_substrate$statistic, 2),
                       ", df = ", kw_substrate$parameter,
                       ", p = ", signif(kw_substrate$p.value, 3))

p.substrate <- 
  ggplot(hill_substratedf, aes(x = direct_substrate, y = Hill_1)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.4, color = "black") +
  labs(x = "", y = "Exponential Shannon Index", caption = caption_text,
       title = "Exponential Shannon Index across substrate types") +

p.substrate
```

# Beta diversity

Phyloseqs (created at the beginning of the script)

```{r}
reef_tss 
morphotype_subs
morphotype_col 
```

## Environmental

Scaled environmental variables are calculated once, across all samples in `reef_tss`, and joined to each subset. This replaces the separate `env_subs_scaled` / `env_col_scaled` objects (which were scaled within each subset) and the `env_scaled` object from correlations_environments.Rmd, which was not loaded in this script. If that script also filters variables or samples, load its output here instead.

```{r}
meta_all <- as(sample_data(reef_tss), "data.frame")

# Check the raw column names match your metadata (temperature, salinity, chla, mean.PO4, DIN)
env_scaled <- meta_all %>%
  transmute(sample_id,
            temp.scaled = as.numeric(scale(temperature)),
            sal.scaled  = as.numeric(scale(salinity)),
            chla.scaled = as.numeric(scale(chla)),
            PO4.scaled  = as.numeric(scale(mean.PO4)),
            DIN.scaled  = as.numeric(scale(DIN)))
```

Merge env_scaled with the metadata of each phyloseq

```{r}
env_cols <- c("sample_id", "site", "site_type", "mat_color", "direct_substrate",
              "substrate_group", "biotic_abiotic")

build_env <- function(ps) {
  as(sample_data(ps), "data.frame") %>%
    select(all_of(env_cols)) %>%
    left_join(env_scaled, by = "sample_id") %>%
    remove_rownames() %>%
    column_to_rownames("sample_id")
}

env      <- build_env(reef_tss)          # all samples
env.subs <- build_env(morphotype_subs)   # substrate subset
env.col  <- build_env(morphotype_col)    # colour subset
```

## Community matrixes

```{r}
# Rows in the same order as the matching env table
community.matx      <- otu_matrix(reef_tss)[rownames(env), , drop = FALSE]
community.matx.subs <- otu_matrix(morphotype_subs)[rownames(env.subs), , drop = FALSE]
community.matx.col  <- otu_matrix(morphotype_col)[rownames(env.col), , drop = FALSE]

# Check that row names match between community and env matrices
stopifnot(identical(rownames(community.matx),      rownames(env)),
          identical(rownames(community.matx.subs), rownames(env.subs)),
          identical(rownames(community.matx.col),  rownames(env.col)))

# Reef and lake subsets (used by the dbRDA sections)
community.matx.reef <- community.matx[env$site_type == "reef", , drop = FALSE]
env.reef            <- env[env$site_type == "reef", , drop = FALSE]
community.matx.lake <- community.matx[env$site_type == "lake", , drop = FALSE]
env.lake            <- env[env$site_type == "lake", , drop = FALSE]

# Lake chunks only run when lake samples are present (this phyloseq contains reefs only)
has_lakes <- nrow(env.lake) > 2
has_lakes
```

## PERMANOVA sites x site type

Uses all samples (site does not depend on morphology). When both site types are present, sites are nested within site type (site_type + site_type:site). With reefs only, the model is site alone.

Note: in the nested model, site_type is tested against permutations of individual samples, not whole sites, so its p-value is optimistic.

```{r nested permanova}
perm <- 9999

nested_formula <- if (n_distinct(env$site_type) > 1) {
  community.matx ~ site_type + site_type:site
} else {
  community.matx ~ site
}

permanova.site.nested <- adonis2(nested_formula,
                                 data = env,
                                 permutations = perm,
                                 method = "bray",
                                 by = "terms")
permanova.site.nested

# Pairwise PERMANOVA between sites, within each site type (BH correction)
pairwise_site.nested <- lapply(split(seq_len(nrow(env)), env$site_type), function(idx) {
  if (n_distinct(env$site[idx]) < 2) return(NULL)
  pairwise.adonis(community.matx[idx, , drop = FALSE],
                  factors    = as.character(env$site[idx]),
                  sim.method = "bray",
                  p.adjust.m = "BH",
                  perm       = perm)
})
pairwise_site.nested <- Filter(Negate(is.null), pairwise_site.nested)
pairwise_site.nested
```

Save pairwise results as dataframes

```{r}
pairwise_site.reef <- to_table(pairwise_site.nested[["reef"]], source_col = FALSE)
pairwise_site.lake <- if (has_lakes) to_table(pairwise_site.nested[["lake"]], source_col = FALSE) else NULL
```

#### Pairwise plot

```{r}
df_all <- bind_rows(pairwise_site.nested, .id = "site_type") %>%
  mutate(pairs = reorder(pairs, R2))   # order by effect size

pairwise_effectsize_site <-
  ggplot(df_all, aes(x = R2, y = pairs, color = p.adjusted < 0.05)) +
  geom_point(size = 4) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey50", `TRUE` = "red")) +
  facet_wrap(~ site_type, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1,
             labeller = labeller(site_type = facet_labels_sitetype)) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
  labs(title = "Pairwise PERMANOVA Results",
       x = "Effect size (R\u00b2)", y = "Pair",
       color = "Significant (BH p<0.05)")
pairwise_effectsize_site
```

## PERMANOVA substrates

```{r}
# Direct substrate
permanova.substrate <- adonis2(community.matx.subs ~ direct_substrate,
                               data = env.subs,
                               permutations = perm,
                               method = "bray", 
                               by = "margin",
                               na.action = na.omit)
permanova.substrate

pairwise_substrate <- pairwise.adonis(x = community.matx.subs,
                                      factors = env.subs$direct_substrate,
                                      sim.method = "bray",
                                      p.adjust.m = "BH",
                                      perm = perm) %>%
  to_table(source_col = FALSE)

# Biotic-abiotic
permanova.biotic <- adonis2(community.matx.subs ~ biotic_abiotic,
                            data = env.subs,
                            permutations = perm,
                            method = "bray", 
                            by = "margin",
                            na.action = na.omit)
permanova.biotic

pairwise_biotic <- pairwise.adonis(x = community.matx.subs,
                                   factors = env.subs$biotic_abiotic,
                                   sim.method = "bray",
                                   p.adjust.m = "BH",
                                   perm = perm) %>%
  to_table(source_col = FALSE)
```

## PERMANOVA color

Note: colour groups are very unbalanced (2-3 mats for lila and red-brown), the same reason the alpha diversity test was not done. Interpret with caution.

```{r}
permanova.color <- adonis2(community.matx.col ~ mat_color,
                           data = env.col,
                           permutations = perm,
                           method = "bray", 
                           by = "margin",
                           na.action = na.omit)
permanova.color

pairwise_color <- pairwise.adonis(x = community.matx.col,
                                  factors = env.col$mat_color,
                                  sim.method = "bray",
                                  p.adjust.m = "BH",
                                  perm = perm) %>%
  to_table(source_col = FALSE)
```

## PERMANOVA save

```{r}
permanova_list <- list(
  "PERMANOVA sites"            = to_table(permanova.site.nested), 
  "PERMANOVA substrate"        = to_table(permanova.substrate),
  "PERMANOVA color morphotype" = to_table(permanova.color),
  "PERMANOVA biotic-abiotic"   = to_table(permanova.biotic), 
  "Pairwise reefs"             = pairwise_site.reef, 
  "Pairwise lakes"             = pairwise_site.lake, 
  "Pairwise substrate"         = pairwise_substrate, 
  "Pairwise biotic-abiotic"    = pairwise_biotic, 
  "Pairwise color morphotype"  = pairwise_color
)
permanova_list <- Filter(Negate(is.null), permanova_list)   # drops lakes when absent
```

Save all in word document

```{r}
doc <- read_docx()

for (nm in names(permanova_list)) {
  doc <- body_add_par(doc, nm, style = "Normal")
  doc <- body_add_flextable(doc, flextable(permanova_list[[nm]]))
  doc <- body_add_par(doc, "")
}

print(doc, target = "outputs/stats/permanovas_pairwise_site_subs_col.docx")
```

## PCoA all

### Bray-Curtis distance matrix

```{r}
bray_dist <- vegdist(community.matx, method = "bray")
```

### PCoA analysis

```{r}
pcoa_result <- cmdscale(bray_dist, eig = TRUE, k = 2)
```

### DF PCoA

```{r}
pcoa_df <- data.frame(
  sample_id = rownames(community.matx),
  Axis1     = pcoa_result$points[, 1],
  Axis2     = -pcoa_result$points[, 2],   # axis flipped for display
  env
)

# % variance explained
var_expl <- round(100 * pcoa_result$eig / sum(pcoa_result$eig), 1)
```

### Plots PCoA

```{r}
pcoa_lake.reef <- 
  ggplot(pcoa_df, aes(x = Axis1, y = Axis2, color = site_type, shape = site)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = lake.reef_color, labels = facet_labels_sitetype, name = NULL) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = shape_sites) +
  stat_ellipse(aes(group = site_type), type = "t", linetype = "dashed", level = 0.95) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(x = paste0("PCoA1 (", var_expl[1], "%)"),
       y = paste0("PCoA2 (", var_expl[2], "%)"),
       title = "PCoA with 95% Confidence Ellipses") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
pcoa_lake.reef
```

```{r}
# Same base plot, labelled by a different variable each time
pcoa_label_plot <- function(label_var, title) {
  ggplot(pcoa_df, aes(x = Axis1, y = Axis2, label = .data[[label_var]], color = site_type)) +
    scale_color_manual(values = lake.reef_color, labels = facet_labels_sitetype, name = NULL) +
    geom_point(size = 2) +
    geom_text_repel(size = 3, max.overlaps = 50) +
    labs(x = paste0("PCoA1 (", var_expl[1], "%)"),
         y = paste0("PCoA2 (", var_expl[2], "%)"),
         title = title) +
    theme_bw()
}

pcoa_lake.reef.site <- pcoa_label_plot("site", "PCoA with Location labels")
pcoa_lake.reef.site

pcoa_lake.reef.subs <- pcoa_label_plot("direct_substrate", "PCoA direct substrate labels")
pcoa_lake.reef.subs

pcoa_lake.reef.col <- pcoa_label_plot("mat_color", "PCoA mat color labels")
pcoa_lake.reef.col
```

# dbRDA reef

Same five predictors as dbRDA all, dbRDA lakes and the partial models below (salinity was missing from this model but was used in the partial models and mentioned in the text).

```{r}
dbrda_reef <- capscale(community.matx.reef ~ temp.scaled + sal.scaled + chla.scaled + PO4.scaled + DIN.scaled,
                       data = env.reef, distance = "bray")
RsquareAdj(dbrda_reef)
summary(dbrda_reef)
```

##Anova

ANOVA test sequential (Type I): results depend on the order of the predictors in the formula. Use by = "margin" to test each predictor after all others.

```{r}
anova(dbrda_reef, permutations = 999)              # overall
anova(dbrda_reef, permutations = 999, by = "axis")  # per axis
anova(dbrda_reef, permutations = 999, by = "terms") # per predictor

plot(dbrda_reef)
```

In reefs: PO4, DIN, and Temp significantly explain the variation. Chl-a and salinity don't (check after rerunning with salinity in the model).

## Save tables

```{r}
# Builds the R2, inertia and ANOVA tables for a dbRDA and saves them as docx
dbrda_tables <- function(model, path) {
  rsq <- RsquareAdj(model)
  rsq_tbl <- data.frame(Metric = c("R2", "Adj_R2"),
                        Value  = c(rsq$r.squared, rsq$adj.r.squared))

  s <- summary(model)
  part_tbl <- data.frame(
    Metric     = c("Total", "Constrained", "Unconstrained"),
    Inertia    = c(s$tot.chi, s$constr.chi, s$unconst.chi),
    Proportion = c(s$tot.chi, s$constr.chi, s$unconst.chi) / s$tot.chi
  )

  anova_tbl <- data.frame(anova(model, by = "terms", permutations = 999)) %>%
    rownames_to_column("Variable")

  save_as_docx("R2"                      = flextable(rsq_tbl),
               "Partitioning of Inertia" = flextable(part_tbl),
               "ANOVA by Terms"          = flextable(anova_tbl),
               path = path)

  list(R2 = rsq_tbl, Partition = part_tbl, Anova_by_terms = anova_tbl)
}

# Own name per model, so the lake tables don't overwrite the reef tables
final_tbl_reef <- dbrda_tables(dbrda_reef, "outputs/stats/dbrda_reefs_anova_r2_inertia.docx")
final_tbl_reef
```

## Partial dbRDA

```{r}

dbrda_temp_reef <- capscale(community.matx.reef ~ temp.scaled + Condition(PO4.scaled + DIN.scaled + chla.scaled + sal.scaled),
                            data = env.reef, distance = "bray")
RsquareAdj(dbrda_temp_reef)
anova(dbrda_temp_reef)

dbrda_din_reef <- capscale(community.matx.reef ~ DIN.scaled + Condition(PO4.scaled + temp.scaled + chla.scaled + sal.scaled),
                           data = env.reef, distance = "bray")
RsquareAdj(dbrda_din_reef)
anova(dbrda_din_reef)

dbrda_po4_reef <- capscale(community.matx.reef ~ PO4.scaled + Condition(temp.scaled + DIN.scaled + chla.scaled + sal.scaled),
                           data = env.reef, distance = "bray")
RsquareAdj(dbrda_po4_reef)
anova(dbrda_po4_reef)
```

## Df for plot

```{r}
dbrda_scores.reef <- scores(dbrda_reef, display = "sites") %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("sample_id")

dbrda_biplot.reef <- scores(dbrda_reef, display = "bp") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("variable")

dbrda_scoresdf.reef <- dbrda_scores.reef %>%
  left_join(env.reef %>% rownames_to_column("sample_id"), by = "sample_id")

# Significance from the reef ANOVA by terms
vectorsig.reef <- dbrda_biplot.reef %>%
  left_join(final_tbl_reef$Anova_by_terms %>%
```
